entries.text: From the tower, a hundred feet up. Whole island at once. Cabin and the boat I woke beside are west. Bell on the northeast headland. Stone circle near the eastern cliffs, just grass in the middle. Bridge over the stream to the west. Pond northwest, forest close to the south, ocean southeast, beach southwest, cliffs southeast. James is climbing down with a sword, a lighter, a snorkel, and twenty coins. The mirror by the trees didn't give me a face. I still don't remember arriving.

reflections.text: Sand underfoot, a boat just up the beach, and the water not far the other way. I'll look at the boat before I decide anything else.
The boat is sound and there's an oar in it, but I'm not ready to leave the sand. The water is only a few steps the other way. I want to see what kind of shore this is.
The sand ends and the water starts. I want a closer look before I put a foot in.
Too far to swim, then. Still, the edge is right here. I want to know if the water is warm.
The water's right at my feet. I'll crouch and put a hand in.
The water didn't tell me anything. If someone else is on this beach, I want to know before I walk inland.
Nobody answered. The cabin is the only place a person would be, so I'm walking up the beach toward it.
Someone answered. A man, northeast, by the stream. I'm not walking to an empty cabin if there's a voice.
He heard me. The stream is northeast, a few minutes' walk. I'll go to him rather than keep shouting across the beach.
I can see someone now, north of me, farther than the stream. I'm not going to the water if the person is standing over there.
Still a long way off. I'll keep walking and see who it is when I'm closer.
He's young, about my age, and he's walking too. There's a fire pit just north of me, but I'm not stopping for it.
Close enough that I can see he's walking, not standing still. I'll keep going until I can talk without shouting.
Fifty feet or so. He's still walking. I'll close the rest of the gap before I say anything.
I walked past where he is. He's south of me now, still moving. I'll call so he looks this way.
I overshot him. He's back toward the beach and still walking. Chasing a moving person is how I just missed him. The bridge is right here. I'll tell him to come to it.
He's stopped. Good. I'll finish the call and then actually go stand on the bridge.
He's standing still, only sixty feet off. No point making him come to the bridge when I can just walk to him.
Twenty feet. He's holding a journal and a pencil, same as me. I'll close the last of it.
I walked to where he was, and he's forty feet off again, standing. Same journal and pencil as me. I'll go to where he actually is.
He's talking, but I'm not close enough to hear the words. I'll keep walking.
He wants to meet at the bridge after all. I'll answer him and go.
He's thirty feet off, right by the bridge, and he isn't moving. This time I can actually get there.
He's right here. Same age, same blank-looking journal and pencil. He said his name is James. I should answer him instead of just standing on the bridge.
I said my name. I'll wait and see if he answers before I fill the quiet.
He asked if I'm okay, how I got here, and whether I want the cabin. I don't remember arriving. The cabin is what I wanted before I heard him, and I'd rather not go alone now.
He's offering his hand. I'll take it. I can finish the rest after.
He already started toward the cabin. The handshake missed. I'll catch up.
He's ahead of me again, already walking toward the cabin. If I just chase his last spot I'll miss him a third time. I'll tell him to wait.
He's pulling farther ahead. Let him hear me before I start after him again.
He didn't wait. The cabin is where we said we'd go, so I'll go there instead of chasing his last footprint again.
He stopped. That's what I asked. I'll go to him instead of walking past him to the door.
He's actually here, and so is a closed chest by the cabin. I'll talk to him before I start opening things.
He's sitting now, with coins in his hand, and the chest beside the door is open and heaped with gold. I haven't touched it. I want to know if he opened it.
He's talking, but I didn't catch the words. I'll stay quiet and listen.
He wants the cabin door, not the gold. That matches what I want. I'll tell him I'm coming.
He's already walking toward the door. I'll go with him instead of standing by the chest.
He's at the door, opening it. I'll be there in a moment.
The door is open. Bed, cold fireplace, a table with a lantern. I'll go in and look at the table.
I'm inside. James is still out by the door. The lantern is right here, half full. I'll look at it before I call him in.
He's inside with me now. The cabin is spare — made bed, empty hearth, a lantern with oil. Nothing that explains either of us. I'll tell him what I see.
I asked him something. I'll give him a moment to answer instead of talking over the quiet.
He didn't answer. He's a few steps off, looking hard at something. I'll go see what it is.
I walked over to see what he was looking at. It's the empty hearth. I'll ask him again, plainly, before I start poking around on my own.
He moved off again without answering, and he's looking hard at something toward the bed. I'll go see what it is, once.
He walked off again without answering. I'm not going to trail him. The bed is right here, and I haven't actually looked at it.
The bed is empty and made, and James has gone again without answering. There's a mirror against a tree outside. I want to see what I look like.
I'm already out the door. The mirror is still ahead, and there's a steel tower with a ladder far to the east. I'll get to the mirror first.
Still heading for the mirror. The forest is close on my left, and James is walking off toward the bridge. I'm not following him.
The glass is clean. I want to see the face that goes with this body.
Inspecting it only told me the frame is wood and the glass is clean. I still haven't seen a face. I'll look into it.
The glass stayed blank. No face, no change. I'm done with the mirror. The steel tower is the thing I haven't gone to.
Still going. The tower is a long way yet, and nobody's out here with me. The forest is close on my right. I'll keep walking.
He's already on the ladder, a few feet up. I still want the tower. I'll keep going.
He's already partway up the tower. There's a stepladder on the grass between me and it, and a stone circle farther east. I'll still go to the tall ladder.
He's well above me already, maybe a quarter of the way up. I'll still go to the foot of the ladder.
Almost at the foot of it. He's a third of the way up. I'll get there and then decide whether to climb.
The rungs are dry and solid, and he's already halfway up. I don't like the height, but I walked all this way to see the platform. I'm going up.
Thirteen feet up. The rungs hold. He's well above me. I'll keep climbing.
Twenty-five feet. Both hands on the rungs. He's still above me. The platform is the reason I started, so I'll keep going.
Forty feet. The ground looks smaller and the rungs still hold. He's near the top. I'll keep going.
Halfway. The ground is a long way down and he's almost at the platform. I'll keep climbing.
Sixty-four feet. He's already standing on the platform. I still can't see what's up there. I'll keep climbing.
Seventy-six feet. Both hands on the rungs, the ground a long way down. He's already on the platform. I'll finish the climb.
He's kneeling at the opening, holding the rail, offering his arm. I'll take it when I get there. Not yet — both hands stay on the rungs until the top.
Almost at the opening. Both hands stay on the rungs until I'm actually there.
I'm up. The whole island is out there — cabin and boat to the west, cliffs and a bell to the northeast, the sea on two sides. I didn't need the arm. I want the railing before I touch anything.
I'm already on the steel. The railing is the far side of this platform, and there's a sword on the table. I'll go to that.
I can't walk across the platform without the world telling me to climb down first. The sword is close enough to look at from here, so I'll do that.
The sword is just a scabbard and a strap. I still want the railing, not the blade. I'll try stepping north across the steel instead of targeting the table.
He finally said something that was actually about this place. I don't want the sword. The bell is the thing that might make a sound. I want a minute up here before I climb down.
He's already holding the sword. The table is empty. I'll finish what I was saying.
He took the sword anyway and started down. Fine. I said I wanted a minute with the view, and I can still see the whole island from here. I'll write it down before I forget the shape of it.
The writing is slow, which is fine. He's already well down the ladder with the sword. The island doesn't move. I'll finish the page.
Still writing. The sea is on two sides and the forest starts just south of the tower. I'll finish the page before I climb down.
Halfway through the page. The forest starts just south of the tower and the sea is still on two sides. I'll finish writing before I climb down.
Still writing. The page is the only thing I can do up here that the ladder doesn't interrupt.
Almost done with the page. I'll let it finish.
Almost done. I'll finish the page, then climb down.
The page is done. I've had the view. The bell is northeast, and I still want to hear it. Down.
Eighty-five feet. Both hands on the rungs. The bell is still northeast, past the stone circle. I'll keep going down.
He's at the bottom, waiting on the bell. I already decided that. Both hands stay on the rungs.
Sixty-three feet. He's waiting at the base. I'll keep both hands on the rungs.
Still on the rungs. The bell hasn't moved. Neither have I, except down.
Halfway down. The bell is still northeast, past the stone circle. I'll keep both hands on the rungs.
Thirty-three feet. The stone circle is closer than the bell, but the bell is what I came down for. I'll keep going.
Eighteen feet. The sword is on the grass now, not on him. I'll get off the ladder, then go to the bell.
Four feet. I'll step off, then go northeast toward the bell.
The sword can stay in the grass. The bell is northeast, past the stone circle. I'm not waiting.
Straight northeast hits the tower. I'll go east around the foundation, then toward the headland.
Clear of the tower. The stone circle is on the way to the headland. I'll cut northeast toward it and look for the bell from there.
The circle is a marker, not the point. If the bell shows itself from there, I'll leave the stones and go to it.
The bell is past the stones, on the headland. I don't need to stop at the circle.
Fifty-three feet. I can hear the grass, not the bell. Not yet.
He's ringing it before I get there. I'll still go. I want to see it, and hear it from close.
The rope is right there. I came for the sound, not for him to announce it. I'll pull it myself.
He already rang it once. I still want my own pull. The rope is in my hands.
It carried. Two rings, his and mine. I'll stand still and listen for an answer before I do anything else.
Nothing back yet. Just the two rings dying out. I'll keep listening.
Still nothing. No shout, no second bell from somewhere else. I'll give it the rest of the wait.
He's talking, but nothing else answers the bell. I'll finish the listen.
He wants another ring. We've already sent two. I'll stay still and listen through his third, in case someone finally answers.
No third ring yet, and no answer. I'll stay through the rest of the wait.
No one answered. Three rings and only us. The sea is east of the headland. I want to see it from up here before the time runs out, and I won't walk off the edge.
East is blocked, probably the frame. I'll go southeast around it and try to see the water without getting near the cliff edge.
The cliffs are east, not under my feet yet. I'll finish this arc and look at the water from the grass.
The water is forty-nine feet east and the drop is closer than that. I'll go partway and stop on the grass.
Rocky ground, the drop fifteen feet off to the northeast, the water beyond that. Close enough. I'll sit and watch it until the time is gone.
The water is there, east, past the drop. I can hear the grass and nothing else. That's enough. I'll stay sitting until it ends.

reflections.text: I’ll start by heading to the stream—water usually tells me about a place.
I’ll let the walk finish—curious how cold the water is.
I want to feel the water and see how it moves here.
I want to feel the current and wake up a bit, then I’ll head for that ladder to see the view.
That woke me up. I’ll go see what the height gives me—heading for the ladder.
Someone else? I’ll call back and head that way if she answers.
Sounds southwest—farther than the cabin. I’ll head that way via the cabin and call again once I’m closer.
Changing course to the wooden bridge to meet her faster.
Keeping pace to the bridge—I’ll wave when I spot her.
I’m on the wooden bridge by the stream—I see you! I’ll meet you halfway.
I keep walking toward her, raising a hand in a wave.
I keep walking toward her and give a clear wave—open posture, easy smile.
I keep heading to her—I'll say hi when I'm close enough to talk without shouting.
I’ll keep walking—close enough soon to talk without shouting.
I keep going to meet her.
She’s just northeast—I’ll jog the rest and talk up close.
On my way! Keep talking—I’ve got you.
On it—heading to the wooden bridge.
She’s right here—no need to sprint past her.
I stay on the bridge and wave her over.
I wait on the bridge, hand raised to wave her in.
I’m glad you found me.
I listen, taking her in up close.
Nice to meet you, Mara. I’ve got the same journal and pencil. I started up on the hill. You okay? Want to head to the cabin together—there’s a chest by the door I’m curious about.
I offer my hand and a steady look; if she’s comfortable, we’ll go check the chest together.
Glad you’re here, Mara. Let’s check that chest by the cabin—maybe there’s something useful. We can compare notes on the way: you said there’s a rowboat and a crate on the beach?
Got it—Mara. Let’s check the chest at the cabin first, then maybe the ladder. Did you notice anything in the crate by the boat on your way up?
Okay—let’s check the chest first.
Let’s open the chest together when we get there.
Almost there. I thought I heard another voice—did you hear that?
Almost there—I see the chest. Mara, I’m by the cabin; come to the chest!
I’ll wait here by the chest—right by the cabin door. Come join me, Mara.
Sorry—here by the chest. I’ll wait; take your time coming up.
I’m here by the chest, Mara—slowing down. I’ll wait so we can open it together.
I sink down beside the chest and wait for Mara, listening for that faint voice again.
Over here, Mara—I’ll wait so we can open it together. You okay to sit a sec?
Hey, Mara. You made it—let’s open this together.
Whoa. That’s… a lot of gold. Gorgeous, but not exactly useful here. Want to feel it? Then maybe we peek in the cabin.
I eye the open chest, amused at how absurd the gold feels here, and decide the cabin matters more.
I’ll finish telling her and then head to the door.
Yeah, I opened it—it's full of gold. I haven’t checked the cabin yet. Let’s do it together. Ready?
Let’s check the door together.
Let’s check the cabin. I’ll try the latch.
Leaving the rest. Come on, Mara—let’s check the door.
I’ll try the latch—let’s see what’s inside.
Handle feels solid—opening it slowly.
Door’s open. I’ll step inside—let’s take a look around: table, lantern, bed, fireplace.
Let’s go in. I’ll check the lantern and table first.
Heading to the table—let’s see if the lantern has oil.
Lantern’s half full—promising. I’ll check the table for drawers or matches. Mara, could you glance by the fireplace for tinder or flint?
Lantern’s half full. I’ll check the fireplace for tinder or tools. Mara, can you see if there’s a tinderbox tucked near the bed frame?
I’m going to take a closer look at the fireplace—see if there’s any tools or a tinderbox tucked nearby. Could you check around the bed frame and under the blanket corners, Mara?

Outside I found the stream, the wooden bridge, and that chest of coins by the cabin—nothing else useful. I kept hearing a faint voice earlier, like an echo. Once I check the hearth up close, maybe we should look up—there’s a platform at the top of the ladder.
Up close now—let me check the hearth and surround, then we can try the ladder platform.
